reviews.text: It tells a tale that would fit right into a lineup of stories from Poe himself.
reviews.author: Joseph Tomastik

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye falls flat in the conventionality of its final, fiery conclusion.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: A superficial story that takes one too many creative liberties.
reviews.author: Ally Ham

reviews.text: Even with the strong performances of Melling, Bale, and the rest of the supporting cast, the mystery doesn’t provide a satisfying resolution despite the complex investigation that centres on the movie.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: Led by Melling, there are strong performances throughout, including a giallo-level turn by Gillian Anderson as Julia Marquis, and the always reliable Robert Duvall as Jean-Pepe, an occult scholar.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: Though overly reliant on its familiar score, The Pale Blue Eye strikes a rare balance between macabre mystery and prestige drama, embedding itself within a middle ground that never ceases to entice and evoke a powerful sense of pathos.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: Here and there, the inherent silliness of it all manages to overpower Cooper’s quest for bleakness.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is beautiful, and its script coherent and clean. While its story may not inspire a second watch, it is a film that relishes in its tone, atmosphere, and aesthetics.
reviews.author: Emma-Jane Betts

reviews.text: Beautifully shot and competently acted, The Pale Blue Eye is worth a watch from the comfort of your own home. However, despite it's best effort, it may not intrigue and entertain as much as it wants to.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: If you have a particular passion for the Gothic, you may find this film appealing despite its flaws.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: Sometimes the journey is enough, even if the destination isn’t quite what we’d hoped for.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: I’ve never been a fan of director Scott Cooper, but this period murder mystery is one of his better films.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: The mood between Bale and his pale-faced literary companion seems as frosty as the wintry weather in this adaptation of Louis Bayard’s 2003 novel... frost, snow, blue light, icy breath — but light on actual detective work and plot.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Bale does what Bale does, inhabiting a brooding, secretive character similar to many he has played in the past, while Melling’s Poe is superb, flirting with camp caricature yet remaining nuanced and unpredictable.
reviews.author: John Townsend

reviews.text: A flurry of impeccable performances, ornately decadent costuming, a carefully choreographed color palette, and painting-perfect cinematography, all spun together by a compelling mystery and one of the best fictionalized Edgar Allan Poe's we've ever seen.
reviews.author: Kimberley Elizabeth

reviews.text: Bale utilizes the heavily mustachioed beardfulness he employs in all his 1800's roles, and while he can chew the scenery with the best of them, he allows Melling's scary-doll, wide-eyed E.A. Poe to upstage him. A plodding but highly engrossing watch.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Beautiful, slow and gloomy, The Pale Blue Eye is a pleasant enough detour for any mystery and gothic devotees, although its flaws might be too glaring for some to ignore.
reviews.author: Gabi Zietsman

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye ultimately feels exactly like an Edgar Allen Poe work. Ravens are present. Death beneath wood floorboards. Tortured souls and dark family secrets. It comes together like a dive into a book that comes alive.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: One's a world-weary alcoholic, the other's a twitchy West Point cadet with literary aspirations. Together, they fight crime.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: It’s a visually wow-inducing whodunit that feels dour and slow at times.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Top notch acting is overcome by an unbelievable, somber plot and overly dark visuals.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: There is something ridiculous, not when it begins, but as it nears its end, which makes one want to quickly forget The Pale Blue Eye... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Cooper’s direction never quite instills a sense of urgency or suspense, leaving the fine cast and promising story to feel underserviced by the script and its execution.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: If it kept its early promise of a macabre deep dive into Poe’s literary universe, via an intricate murder mystery, this would have been an outstanding thriller.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: There’s a real dearth of Hollywood adaptations of Edgar Allan Poe’s work. Unfortunately, The Pale Blue Eye is far from the film that Poe deserves.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: It is built as a thriller with gothic ink that points out its mystery through an inane narrative that leaves the most conventional traces of detective fiction on the surface. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Bale’s compelling performance and chemistry with Melling’s Poe will carry viewers through the less enthralling moments in the second act. The mystery takes awhile to build, but the third act provides some unexpected twists.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Much as the cast tries, however, none overcome the story’s outrageous elements delivered in a slow and meticulous manner rather than with compelling cinematic excitement.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: There is a potentially intriguing mystery at its heart but the plodding The Pale Blue Eye ultimately doesn't make the most of its interesting setup.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: An impeccably created tale of love, madness and death that rewards patience. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Given the story’s flat complications, it’s frustrating how magnificent the movie appears when Bale is silhouetted in his top hat amid the Hudson Valley fog.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: I felt like I had been cheated.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: I found the mystery itself a bit dull, but I liked the setting of this and the character Christian Bale is playing.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: It’s a dark, lurid and weird place where this unexpected gem exists, at times, quite comfortably.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: It’s made by a good director, has a fine cast, a compelling plot and an intriguing historical link to Poe’s fascination with death. Such elements make it worth watching, even if it does become predictable and silly by the end.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Up until the film’s nutty climax and elongated confessional, Scott Cooper’s film is a reminder that Christian Bale always shows up to provide something interesting even when the filmmaking is tedious at best.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Cooper's film is beautifully shot, but the story is boring and fails to justify its long runtime. Worst of all: everyone is on autopilot save Melling and Anderson. The film needed more of their kooky energy.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: The direction, production aesthetic, and performances are all top-class and make The Pale Blue Eye a tremendously enjoyable dark thriller. Watch it for the mood, and for Harry Melling’s brilliant performance.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: A pretty study February chiller with snow everywhere and Henry Melling doing his best Foghorn Dreadhorn impression.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: It’s a fine Hollywood film. But Poe’s mysteries aren’t so easy to pin down.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: The resolution and reveals in the final act come so fast, and in such rapid fire, they lose some of their impact. It almost feels like Cooper was just ready to be done with this tale, and frankly, so were we.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Well balanced cinematography adds depth to this clever mystery and offers some strong performances by [Christian] Bale and [Harry] Melling.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: This period mystery has a few flaws in its logic, but its stellar cast, some good twists, and a crisp, wintry atmosphere add up to a sturdy, bleak film that should pair well with a hot mug of cocoa.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The patient, dark understatement of the whole adventure worked for me and felt in concert with the quiet and shadowed world it portrays.
reviews.author: Alison Lanier

reviews.text: I think for those that need something to watch with the main two characters showing off their talent with a backdrop of drab and dull characters, this is it.
reviews.author: Quinton Roberts

reviews.text: Too serious for its own good, and with a visual palette and pace that both suggests a frozen hinterland, it’s not so much a whodunit as it is a whybother.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: The movie goes on too long, and it ends on a note so muted you wonder what became of all the fun buildup that preceded it. This is the real mystery.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: For viewers weary of horror that embraces the minimalist and dystopian, The Pale Blue Eye -- chock-full of emotion, mystery, and romance from a bygone era -- is a welcome sight indeed.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: Long on atmosphere but short on logic and excitement, Scott Cooper’s brooding adaptation of Louis Bayard’s 2003 historical mystery wastes an exceptional cast on a tale that grows increasingly silly as it plods to an exasperating conclusion.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: The storytelling is plodding, nothing Poe-tic about it, but Poe himself is a lively, eccentric presence.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: Hey, if we had “Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter,” why not “Edgar Allan Poe: CSI sleuth”?
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The slightly underwhelming mystery plotting and general crime-novel luridness don’t limit The Pale Blue Eye as much as they should, because of the engaging lead characters and the wintry landscape they inhabit.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye, a bad movie encumbered by a good cast, probably came across better in outline than it does onscreen.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: It’s a film that, on an aesthetic level, casts an eerie spell. Shame about its story, though.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: At over two hours, the film feels even longer and misses the opportunity to make this killer case all that interesting.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: ... A homage to the spirit of Poe's writing more than a mise-en-scène of any of his stories. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: It's gorgeous to look at and the period details are on point, but The Pale Blue Eye is a dull, interminable slog that lacks a compelling mystery and offers one too many conclusions.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: People while watching this film might wonder why Bale agreed to support the growth of a literary powerhouse by acting as a sort of "second fiddle" to another character. In the final fifteen minutes of the movie, you will get the answer
reviews.author: Abhishek Srivastava

reviews.text: It's a missed opportunity to introduce an iconic figure like Poe into the fold and not have any payoff whatsoever — it's like clickbait historical fiction casting.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: Cooper perfectly captures the chilly terrain of the Hudson Highlands and fills the twisting story with a gothic atmosphere befitting the poet who walks within the pages.
reviews.author: Jenn Adams

reviews.text: A highly promising but ultimately uneven period mystery drama
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: It’s a slow burn of a movie, with a great twist, which will ultimately leave viewers wanting more.
reviews.author: Ryan Britt

reviews.text: A serious disappointment.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye hasn’t got its heart in the right place, perhaps it should check for it underneath the floorboards.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Bayard’s historical saga drips with exquisite prose and finds beauty in the macabre with a dark and twisted story. The film executes that story well but with none of the poetry and nuance that the book has in spades.
reviews.author: Erin Allen

reviews.text: It doesn’t say anything new about Poe, and it gets frankly goofy for a while, but it’s mostly diverting and comes to a pretty decent conclusion.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye closes as a mystery made up of intriguing, alluring parts that don’t always come together fully, but on their own demonstrate the skill of everyone involved.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Perhaps most frustrating about The Pale Blue Eye’s languid atmosphere is that the film often scratches at greatness.
reviews.author: Aurora Amidon

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is a beautifully atmospheric and sometimes surprising period whodunit that falls prey to some disappointing crime story tropes.
reviews.author: Kyle Logan

reviews.text: Florid yet frosty...Since writer/director Scott Cooper fails to establish a shred of empathy for any of the dour characters, the bleak story-telling is a big of a slog.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: “The Pale Blue Eye” is a winner for Netflix and one more reason that audiences for these kinds of grown-up stories are heading to streaming services rather than the multiplexes.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Come for the great cast but don't expect great thrills with this turbid adaptation of Louis Bayard's 'The Pale Blue Eye.'
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: … a unique and unforgiving bit of Gothic horror.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: …The Pale Blue Eye is a fairly cold-hearted and mechanical story that springs to life when the spirit of Edgar Allan Poe is evoked…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The pace moves as sluggish as walking in deep and thick snow, making its 128-minute runtime feel like a tedious crawl that drags on and on.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: We’ve got to chip through a whole lot of frost to get to the firey heart of this Gothic whodunit.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: The film's eerie and atmospheric setting and cinematography does a lot of the heavy lifting until the ultimate twists that you will either go with, or roll your eyes at.
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: The movie promises more than it ultimately delivers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: With its wintry aesthetic, candlelit hallways, and gothic pedigree, The Pale Blue Eye could stand to be a lot pulpier and more fun than it is. As it stands, the film’s fealty to its period-piece trappings make it disappointingly dry.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Those who are intrigued by the history of Old New York, and Poe, might respond to the film’s portrait of both. Those who insist on stories making total sense might need to chase The Pale Blue Eye with a cask of amontillado.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: It’s a troupe in service of a story that’s only barely satisfying when it finally decides to tie up loose ends. The real pleasure, it turns out, was always meant to be the weirdos we met along the way.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: You won’t necessarily get goosebumps, but you might feel a slight chill of surprise; English-language Netflix projects rarely feel as menacing as this, even if the danger more often than not leers from a distance.
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: A mystery that’s more about mood than ingenuity. But the chill you feel in your bones may actually enhance the suspense; Cooper clearly understands that mysteries live or die on their atmosphere.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: “The Pale Blue Eye” isn’t biography but invention, and Melling is the merry wind-up toy at its center. Watch it for him and for the way Bale anchors the younger man’s performance to the movie’s here and now.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: It evokes the eeriness inherent in Poe’s work, the thumbscrew tension of detective examinations, and the romantic despair of Gothic literature.
reviews.author: Tony Sokol

reviews.text: “The Pale Blue Eye,” based on a novel by Louis Bayard, is an atmospheric and deliberate whodunit that doesn’t depend too heavily on perhaps the greatest mystery writer of all time in a supporting role.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: While it drags slightly, THE PALE BLUE EYE is a proper Gothic murder mystery that pays respectful homage to Edgar Allen Poe.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: The best part of the movie is the last 20 minutes, and that’s not something you want to hear about a film that’s over two hours long.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: A solidly built mystery, The Pale Blue Eye crumbles in the underwhelming third act, which doesn’t deliver a resolution that fits the complexity of the crime presented. While still a very well-made film, this is not nearly what I had hoped it would be.
reviews.author: Alex Maidy

reviews.text: The mystery itself never quite comes to a boil the way you might hope. Despite its hearty premise and good setup, it feels like something was lost between paper and screen.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Christian Bale tries to solve a murder at West Point, circa 1830, with the help of young cadet Edgar Allen Poe (Harry Melling). But what should be a gothic mesmerizer ends up a dreary exercise to doom and gloom that’s an endurance test for audiences.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Whether it’s an engaging tale or a soporific yarn will likely vary from viewer to viewer. While I found it handsome, I struggled to follow along.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: It's smart and well done and features one of the best one-on-one scenes I've had the pleasure to watch in a while.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: A gothic mystery that not only owes a great creative debt to the stories of Edgar Allen Poe but also features him as a supporting character, director Scott Cooper's latest is an inherently goofy movie undone by delusions of grandeur.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: It's a well-crafted Gothic tale with solid performances, but its pacing won't be to all tastes and could leave you feeling cold.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: A slow burner, for which you must enter with patience, enjoying the ingredients; in this case, the acting work of Bale and Melling, and the dark, greyish, gothic atmosphere, as depressive as the temperament of its protagonists. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: It goes completely off the rails in the final preposterous scenes. Still, “The Pale Blue Eye” is involving for most of its two-hour, ten-minute running time.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: It was the mood that sucked me in and held my attention. The cold, dark, snowy and haunting, gothic 1800's New England atmosphere is quite incredibly rendered through the costuming, cinematography, and Howard Shore's score.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: Writer-director Scott Cooper’s adaptation of Louis Bayard’s novel is a strange, crafty murder mystery laden with gothic atmosphere, tight plot turns, and a fantastic supporting ensemble.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye, based on the novel by Louis Bayard, is meant to be a gothic whodunit by design. However, it will hardly inspire a second thought.
reviews.author: Ferdosa Abdi

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye intrigues with fascinating character dynamics and occult themes. The narrative eventually stumbles with pacing issues and a perplexing, twist-laden third act. Harry Melling carries the film with an enthusiastic performance.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Atmosphere can only carry you so far, and despite the appeal of another haunted, brooding performance from Bale and memorable work from a show-stealing Melling, the film never quite achieves the potential of its impressive pedigree.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Subtly says something meaty about the military mindset, family lineage and the hazards of prolonged grief.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: As for the mystery, it proves captivating from beginning to end, its twists and turns logical and surprising, the denouement clever and haunting.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eyes may look the part of a taut mystery, but its narrative drastically underachieves in its pursuits.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is a handsomely mounted, pulpy murder mystery, with some fine performances, but its methodical pace and bleak nature fail to break free of the movie’s gothic shackles.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Christian Bale’s weary detective mentors a young Edgar Allen Poe in a stylish gothic murder mystery.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye moves at a tired pace with an overabundance of dialogues that turn this into an incredibly monotonous and extenuating experience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: This is a respectable effort and reasonably rewarding watch that has its good points...
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: A stylish and smart telling of what is at heart macabre malarkey.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye marks the film-maker’s third collaboration with Bale. Many other actors mill about to no real avail. It’s not a career high for any party, but it’ll serve well enough as silly Christmas entertainment.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: While pacing and believability issues in “The Pale Blue Eye” cannot be overlooked, this finely made period mystery’s virtues should still be savored.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is far from perfect, but it’s still worth a watch if you’re a fan of crime procedurals. It’ll pass the time pleasantly enough until something better comes along.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: “The Pale Blue Eye” is held together by the performances, specifically Henry Melling’s detracted interpretation of Edgar Allan Poe’s lore and mythology.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is a well-constructed gothic mystery bolstered by solid performances but can't quite stick the landing in a muddled third act.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: It’s dripping with a dark mood and atmosphere which makes it a wickedly fun watch, but this isn’t quite Cooper’s best work.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye wastes a genuinely thought-provoking and intriguing premise.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: While the picture looks wonderfully atmospheric throughout, with its frostbitten monochromes and consumptive colour palette, the story disintegrates into a lurid and rather silly final act.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Director Scott Cooper and actor Christian Bale eat crow in this hum drum Edgar Allen Poe whodunnit.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: If you’re looking for a moody detective story, Eye is a reasonable option, even if the ending is very silly.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: With a commanding performance by Bale, exquisite exterior cinematography wrought from natural lighting by Masanobu Takayanagi, and a committed turn by Melling as Poe, it’s unfortunate that The Pale Blue Eye is a meandering disappointment.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Thankfully, strong performances and a striking ending lift it beyond its shortcomings. There’s a gem here if viewers are willing to find it.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Can be enjoyed if you can somehow overcome how it goes off the tracks.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Scott Cooper’s film starts well enough and establishes its gothic atmosphere nicely. But an overripe plot overtakes it midway through.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Despite a few stumbles as macabre as a few of Poe's fictions, The Pale Blue Eye emerges in a void and hopeless atmosphere of existential horror, as righteous as it is bitter. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pedro Paunero

reviews.text: Even a great cast can't save The Pale Blue Eye, a gloomy melodramatic story...
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It’s a handsome adaptation, albeit with an unnecessary bit of literary celebrity dragged alongside it.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: There’s a self-serious quality to the film too that ensures it stops short of being the compelling serial killer thriller it could have been.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The film looks so dark that it is often hard to figure out what is going on... [But] The Pale Blue Eye as a whole works because of Christian Bale’s performance.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is a soberly told Gothic whodunnit, laced with lurid sights which imprint themselves into Poe’s future fiction, with a final twist which satisfyingly remakes everything and everyone we’ve seen.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: It's all rather dense and meandering, but the stylish flights of fancy are intriguing, as is the heightened drama between the characters. And writer-director Scott Cooper creates striking visuals that hold the attention.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Clocking in at more than two hours, The Pale Blue Eye (the title is from a line in one of Poe’s works) lumbers when it should lunge.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Its plot is riddled with holes and its ending is overcooked, but it’s packed with terrific actors and achieves the light chill of a Christmas ghost story. Not one Poe would have been proud to write, but perhaps the sort of thing he’d read on holiday.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: An appealingly icy, moody, twisty, Gothic fiction work rooted in the same themes that Poe explored
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Maybe, in truth, it never really does get going. But the story’s stately pace is part of the attraction, and perhaps key to its pleasurably somber tone.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is all at once a melancholic romance, a revenger’s tragedy, and an intriguing mystery. Its one problem, though, is that it comes with a glacial pace to match its wintry setting.
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: A captivating young soul named Edgar Allan Poe steals the picture, as poetically played by Harry Melling (of previous "Harry Potter" fame).
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye isn't a particularly bad film, but it is an unfortunately dull and self-serious one.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: While this stylish and evocative historical whodunit boasts a deep and talented cast, it lacks the suspense and narrative momentum to resonate more deeply.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Even when the 19th century mystery takes some insanely big dramatic swings, Bale is immersed in his performance.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Harry Melling has an uncanny gift for revealing character; he's extraordinary in a classical way. The attention to period detail is intoxicating, and the canny twists, riveting to the final frame.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Scott Cooper, while still adept at directing performance, remains shamefully unable to mold his characters into something resembling a story, leaving too many themes and ideas on the table for his movie to work.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: It gets much darker than I anticipated and excels at maintaining an air of sophisticated drama while also delving into some horror corners. A solid piece all-around.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: A class act from start to finish.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Fails to engage or entertain on even the most basic of levels, a misfire by any other name and a major disappointment to Poe’s fans.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: The movie honors the real-life figure who would, among other things, become the arguable creator of the American detective story, while in its own right turning a shudder-inducing light on the darker recesses of the human heart.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is a period procedural with mood to spare.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: An overlong, leaden and unsubtle drama that can’t even be lifted by its stellar cast.
reviews.author: Nikki Baughan

reviews.text: If you put aside the frankly risible big reveal, the film still manages to be smarter and more original than most of the countless B movies produced by Hollywood right now.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: The entire story is shot through with the same sense of dread and foreboding that emanates from so much of Poe’s writing, which is only heightened further by Poe’s presence within the narrative.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Poe is a far more intriguing and engaging character than the man doing most of the investigative work.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is a character-driven two-hander that’s worth seeing, though some casting choices betray eventual plot turns.
reviews.author: Rob Owen

reviews.text: An unpredictable, exceedingly suspenseful thriller that’ll send more shivers down your spine than an ice-pack on your back, The Pale Blue Eye is filmmaking at its finest.
reviews.author: Caffeinated Clint

reviews.text: While perhaps it lacks the clarity of language that marks the work of Edgar Allan Poe, Cooper finds poetry in his own way.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: A would-be-macabre mystery about hearts being ripped out, is a flatlined pulse and a puzzling absence of red meat.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: A drama with good and particular qualities rather than one that’s genuinely exciting.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye is an engaging and stylish murder mystery with a talented cast that can keep people interested when the movie's pacing sometimes drags. A 'reveal' scene looks clumsy, but the movie is an overall worthy version of Louis Bayard's novel.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: It’s beautiful writing and impeccable acting in a perfectly bleak and maudlin movie.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It’s a prototypical mystery about the prototypical mystery, and that’s not exactly clever when simply laid out plain.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Twists and turns do not always a compelling drama make.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: A clean and neat visual palette gives an expensive look to a boring soap with pretentious scenes, unrefined dialogue, out-of-tune editing, and an exaggerated running time... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: A handsome murder mystery with a neat literary twist and an impressive turn from Harry Melling, but which is overcast by the gloominess of its protagonist and the implausibility of its revelations.
reviews.author: Dan Jolin

reviews.text: And yet Cooper the writer is clearly not trusted by Cooper the director, who shoots this ripe malarkey with a slow and earnest gaze, like a Hammer horror gone social realist.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye may be too frigid to thaw out the full potential of its premise, but this well-furnished Netflix whodunnit still has some fun tapping into the cleverest aspect of the Louis Bayard novel from which it’s been adapted.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: This is a film wonderfully grounded in its time and space, where you hear creaking wooden floorboards and owls hooting and darkness cloaks everything. You feel the 1830s and the greasy, unkempt hair and heavy woolen uniforms.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: Technically speaking, like all of Cooper’s films, The Pale Blue Eye is visually appealing, but is hobbled by a dependence on basic ideas and inspirations, which leads to nowhere but bland artistry.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The best movie yet made about Edgar Allan Poe solving Edgar Allan Poe mysteries.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: It’s one of those handsomely mounted period pieces that should get under your skin; instead, it slumps from scene to scene with little momentum or tension, remaining just this side of inert.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: "The Pale Blue Eye" is a fictional tale that plays like an episode of "Law & Order" that was set in the 1830s.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye holds together remarkably as a gothic piece of horror.
reviews.author: Matthew Monagle

reviews.text: There’s a final destination from Bayard worth waiting for, giving Cooper another interesting study of horror as it emerges in many forms.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: You may start the film by saying you’ve seen this all before, but by the end, Cooper makes it clear that you haven’t seen anything yet.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: This bloody mash up of Christian Bale and Edgar Allan Poe never gets off the ground.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: The unrelentingly bleak material fails to provide more than a straightforward whodunit with a tacked-on reveal relying on frustrating contrivances. We don’t see its biggest twist coming—and, as it turns out, that’s the problem.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Despite the gloom-inflected atmosphere there is little here that actually feeds our fascination with Poe and the macabre mystique he became famous for.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: What "The Pale Blue Eye"... may lack in fully propulsive storytelling and consistent narrative focus is more than made up for by its handsome physical production and gorgeous camerawork.
reviews.author: Gary Goldstein

reviews.text: It’s an entertaining piece of counter-factual noir.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Lavishly appointed and stodgy as week-old Christmas pudding, “The Pale Blue Eye” is a pulpy murder mystery bristling with florid dialogue and supernatural flourishes.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: Just good enough to be a disappointment.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye hits a plateau in its gothic horror storytelling and never musters convincing tension to break from it.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Writer/director Scott Cooper adapts Louis Bayard's novel about a fictional mystery which shaped future works by Edgar Allan Poe from the inside out, two character studies exposing as much about the other as themselves.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It may be Cooper’s best historical film, and perhaps that’s because there’s a distinct melancholy to it that is etched into the bones of Virginia’s finest—just like Poe.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: The film often feels like one of the corpses in its story: cold, lifeless, and without a heart.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: By the time the credits roll, The Pale Blue Eye has not improved on simply curling up in bed with a good book and letting one’s own imagination fill in the blanks.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Filled with surprising twists and turns, incredible cast chemistry, and some of the best set and costumes designs of the year. Bale & Melling are phenomenal on screen together. This one warrants multiple watches, which is rare.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Alas, we can only ponder, weak and weary, over what that better film could have been.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: It’s a compelling endeavor to imagine what Edgar Allen Poe would do if he was a character in a world inspired by his own creation, but the artistic divide between Scott Cooper’s latest film and the macabre wonders of the author himself is quite a chasm.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

reviews.text: The Pale Blue Eye remains an effective gothic horror, bolstered by the addition of Poe and the militaristic setting.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The way the story plays out, though, is enthralling and I did not see the final big twist coming. That makes for a pretty good mystery
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Christian Bale anchors this stolid, darkly beautiful period crime procedural about a series of grisly murders at the pre-Civil War United States Military Academy.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

synopsis: West Point, 1830. In the early hours of a gray winter morning, a cadet is found dead. But after the body arrives at the morgue, tragedy becomes savagery when it's discovered that the young man's heart has been skillfully removed. Fearing irreparable damage to the fledgling military academy, its leaders turn to a local detective, Augustus Landor (Christian Bale), to solve the murder. Stymied by the cadets' code of silence, Landor enlists the help of one of their own to pursue the case, an eccentric cadet with a disdain for the rigors of the military and a penchant for poetry -- a young man named Edgar Allan Poe (Harry Melling).
